title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: V is a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic (0,p), with perfect residue field k and fraction field L. W = W(k) (Witt vectors) sits inside V, and K = Frac W sits inside L.

Grothendieck considers a category C defined inside the filtered (or graded) F-crystals over V, up to isogeny. It is Q_p-linear and tannakian; the margin notes are 'Q_p-linéaire', '½ simple' (semi-simple?) and 'gr. dériv.' (derived group?). C carries two structures:
(a) A fibre functor Φ to F-crystals over k up to isogeny. These are pairs (E,F) with E a finite-dimensional K-vector space and F a σ-linear endomorphism admitting an invariant lattice, i.e. effective F-isocrystals.
(b) A filtration on Φ⊗_K L.
So the objects are what are now called (effective) filtered Dieudonné modules / filtered φ-modules.

A crossed-out line notes that Φ does not identify C with a category of K-linear representations; Φ is a K-valued fibre functor on a Q_p-linear category, i.e. not neutral over K.

He then posits a 'fundamental functor' T_p : C → Mod_f(π, Q_p), with π = Gal(L̄/L). This is the 'foncteur mystérieux' from Barsotti–Tate groups/crystals to p-adic Galois representations. T_p would give a Q_p-valued fibre functor, hence by Tannaka duality an equivalence C ≅ Rep_{Q_p}(G) for a pro-algebraic group G over Q_p, the 'Galois group' of C.

The problem served is to understand the mysterious functor tannakianly: the essential image is a neutral tannakian category over Q_p. Its comparison with the crystal fibre functor Φ (a torsor of isomorphisms between fibre functors) is exactly what Fontaine's period ring B_cris later realised.
errors: The tannakian category of filtered isocrystals in the image of the mysterious functor (crystalline/admissible objects) is not semisimple, if '½ simple' means the category is semisimple. The note may instead refer to the derived group of G ('gr. dériv.'); this is ambiguous.

T_p as a functor on all filtered F-isocrystals is not defined. One must restrict to the (weakly) admissible ones (Colmez–Fontaine 2000), and the functor is contravariant/covariant depending on conventions. The note leaves C's precise definition open.

ideas.what: Effective F-isocrystals over perfect k described as (E, σ-linear F) with an F-stable lattice
ideas.modern_name: effective F-isocrystals / Dieudonné modules up to isogeny
ideas.where_published: Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (ICM 1970; Montréal lectures 1974)

ideas.what: Filtered F-isocrystals: F-isocrystal over K plus a filtration on its base change to L
Fundamental functor T_p from filtered crystals to p-adic Galois representations of Gal(L̄/L)
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck's mysterious functor; Fontaine's V_cris (crystalline representations)

ideas.what: Viewing the category as tannakian over Q_p via T_p, with Galois group G pro-algebraic; second non-neutral fibre functor Φ over K
ideas.modern_name: tannakian group of crystalline representations; period torsor Isom(ω_cris, ω_et) ↔ Spec B_cris
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano (1972, tannakian F-isocrystals), Fontaine, Deligne
ideas.where_published: Tannakian formalism of this sort appears in Saavedra's thesis (Grothendieck's student); not sure Grothendieck published this specific framing

missed.claim: An early (c.1970) explicit tannakian framing of the mysterious functor. Its image is to be Rep_{Q_p}(G) of a pro-algebraic 'Galois group' of the category of filtered F-crystals, alongside the crystal fibre functor Φ over K. This anticipates viewing p-adic comparison as a comparison of fibre functors (period torsor), though the idea became standard via Saavedra/Fontaine/Deligne.
missed.quote: Le foncteur fondamental fournit un foncteur T_p : C → Mod_f(π, Q_p) ... C ≅ Rep_{Q_p}(G), G étant un groupe pro-algébrique sur Q_p
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: documents Grothendieck's own tannakian view of the crystalline–étale comparison at the time of the ICM 1970 talk. It is not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: A clear sketch of the mysterious-functor problem in tannakian language with two fibre functors. Historically nice, but the problem is famous and the tannakian treatment of F-isocrystals is in Saavedra's thesis; there are no new results.
transcription_corrections: Top margin annotations read 'gr. dériv.' and 'Q_p-linéaire' (circled), and '½ simple' next to 'tannakienne'; 'Δ' is inserted above 'fibre'.
'vect. Witt' labels the inclusion W→K (W = Witt vectors), with W ⊂ V over K ⊂ L as a commutative square.
The crossed-out passage reads roughly: 'le foncteur Φ (pas d'identification de C à la catégorie des repr. lin. sur K ...) (en oubliant la filtration)'; 'Weil[?]' is uncertain.
Last line: 'groupe pro-algébrique' with a struck-through intermediate word; the final reading is pro-algébrique sur Q_p.
In a), 'fibre Φ' is the label of the functor to F-crystals over k.
